sourceRefs.summary: Run-contract target that explains why this generated contract exists.
Approved reliability priority and exact product resumption order.

verification: codex execpolicy check against audited allow and deny examples
node --test focused loop-status and Stop-hook suites
skill quick validation for modified Theseus loop skills
allowedWork: Audit and safely consolidate user-level and KP-project Codex rules, configuration, trusted hooks, repeatable check runners, loop-status reporting, loop skills, repository collaboration instructions, and their focused tests.
Modify user-level Codex configuration and skills only for the explicitly approved reliability behavior; keep backups and validate syntax before replacement.
disallowedWork: Do not enable danger-full-access, arbitrary shell or node execution, broad destructive command approval, or approval_policy=never.
Do not modify KP product runtime, animation behavior, roadmap drafts, cross-domain thread drafts, or the user-authored untracked design documents.
goal: Make routine KP development effectively interruption-free while preserving sandbox safety, require explicit reasons for every early loop stop, and expose durable exact loop and slice progress across sessions.
commitCadence: Commit each independently reversible repository unit; record external Codex configuration changes with durable evidence but do not mix them with unrelated project files.
stopConditions: H1 TARGET-DRIFT: stop if a configuration or rules write would target any path other than the audited user Codex layer, trusted KP project layer, approved skills, or KP repository.
H2 POLICY-UNSAFE: stop if rules validation cannot exclude broad destructive, arbitrary shell, or arbitrary node approval.
H3 USER-OVERLAP: stop if required repository edits overlap unrelated user-authored files.
H4 HOOK-LOOP: stop if the Stop hook can recurse, block legitimate completion, mutate product state, or cannot fail open safely.
H5 VALIDATION: stop if Codex configuration, execpolicy, skill, hook, or repository tests fail without a bounded in-scope repair.
H6 AUTHORITY: stop if an external write or policy change requires authority beyond the user approval in this request.
